analogs.covers: The main animal and the whole day: a big seabird with long narrow wings that keeps one ledge on a sea cliff for years, rests and sleeps there among its colony, sets out on long fishing trips along the coast and over the shelf sea, plunges from height into the water, chases its fish underwater with its wings and flies home to the same ledge every time

The time under water and on the rock: a diving fisher that swims after its fish deep below the surface, sits on rocks and ledges with its wings spread to dry and roosts in colonies with water all around

headline: A gannet with a cormorant's dive: one ledge on the sea cliffs as home, long fishing trips along the coast, deep dives for fish and always back to the same rock.

setting.label: Sea cliffs, coasts and the shallow sea, with one home ledge
setting.note: Your home ledge sits in the sea cliffs of the Coastal Bluffs, or on a rock of the Volcano Islands. From there you fly long fishing trips along the coast and over the near sea: Tallbrush Coasts and Kelp Vale to the north, Palm Islands, the Stonebed Shoal, the Mudflats and the East Passage to the east and south-east. The Abyssal Depths are a rare, far trip. The wet woods and bogs inland are on the profile map, but for you they are only a flight path. Courtship at Ripple Beach and nesting at Ocean Pillars follow the profile.

playsLike: You are the cliff fisher. Your home is one ledge on the sea cliffs, and you spend a lot of time there: resting, preening, drying your spread wings and sleeping in short turns, because the water below is dangerous. When you get hungry, you set out on a long fishing trip along the coast and a little out to sea, scanning the surface from above. When you spot fish, you fold your wings, plunge in and chase them deep under water, then shake off, take off again and fly on. Fish and shellfish are almost all you eat. After every trip you fly home to the same ledge. When fishing gets boring, you allow yourself some fun: harassing a herbivore on the beach or dive-bombing a kill. At night, with up to four of you, you may hunt sleeping prey up to Medium; your favourite is Lurdusaurus at your own cliffs.

why.text: The profile opens with a Tropeognathus that "specialized in a diet of fish, diving into the water to snatch prey with precision", and later says they "prefer, ultimately, to exist on a diet of fish and shellfish". Gannets and cormorants eat almost nothing but fish.
"Its lifestyle was likely social, with flocks congregating along shorelines or nesting in cliffs, much like modern seabirds." Gannets crowd onto the ledges of sea cliffs and sea stacks.

"Tropeognathus are typically less active during the daytime, where they will find rocks and cliffsides to temporarily construct nests where they will rest." They "prefer to sleep somewhere surrounded by water - ideally a rock, small island, or coastal cliffside".

They are "often spotted diving in and out of the water with the ability to fly even when drenched" and pick up "shells and crustaceans from either the ocean floor or along the coast". A gannet plunges and then swims after its fish with its wings; a cormorant chases fish deep below the surface.
They "bask for short periods of time, extending their wings to dry them out in the sun": the cormorant on its rock (official inspiration: cormorant).

"Tropeognathus are wary especially of many semi-aquatic species, but especially Deinosuchus & Sarcosuchus", "recognizing the potential threat they pose to fishing Tropeognathus." The Tylosaurus profile adds that it kills Tropeognathus "when they dive for food". Danger waits in the water, so you rest up on the rock.

"They spend the entirety of their lives in coastal and sea-based regions", and after nesting the cluster moves on "to comb the coastlines". Gannets fly hundreds of kilometres along the coast on one fishing trip.

notLike: The profile calls Tropeognathus nomadic. Your home ledge is a roost, not a territory: you never claim or defend it, the rest of your cluster may roost beside you, and when the cluster moves on along the coast after nesting, you may pick a new home ledge further along.
Eating almost only fish is a choice of this guide. The profile also allows hunting at night, carcasses, bones, fruit and insects.
The profile says Tropeognathus spend about half their lives in water. For you that means fishing, diving and bathing; you rest and sleep on the rock, not on the waves.
Gannets fish by day and never hunt big animals; your hunts on healthy animals happen only at night, with up to four of you.
twist: The real Tropeognathus was most likely a soaring fisher that snatched fish from the water and landed as little as possible. As a gannet, you are that fisher, plus the deep dives the profile allows.
